title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All Directors, officers, senior management and other employees, consultants and contractors of the Group. Subject to the inside information ban, the short-term/speculative dealing ban, and the hedging ban on unvested/holding-locked plan securities; no general pre-clearance regime.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, other key management personnel, and other persons who regularly possess Inside Information and have been advised by the Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions. Subject to Blackout Periods, a prior-approval requirement for all dealing (in or out of Blackout Periods), an absolute ban on margin lending and on third-party financial products over Company securities, and obligations regarding Connected Persons.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company (other than the Chair of the Board); a subset of Restricted Persons distinguished only by their dealing approval being given by the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; a Restricted Person distinguished only by their dealing approval being given by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Restricted Person (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, or dependants), and any company or other entity the Restricted Person can control.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other period as a Blackout Period for Restricted Persons at its absolute discretion, subject to applicable law; separately, the Company may notify any Employee that they must not deal in securities for a specified period or until further notice. Confidentiality of either is not expressly addressed, though a refusal or revocation of dealing approval must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Absolute ban 'at any time' on dealing in third-party financial products created over or associated with Company securities, naming derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference, with no clearance route; only Company securities forming a component of a listed portfolio or index product are excepted.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not deal at any time in financial products such as derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps, contracts for difference or other financial products issued or created over or associated with Company securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.

rules.detail: The express ban on third-party financial products (4.7) is confined to Restricted Persons; other Employees dealing in such products are not addressed by this Policy outside the general insider trading law.
Absolute ban applying to all Employees on hedging plan securities before vesting.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Absolute ban applying to all Employees on hedging plan securities while subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction under the plan.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Although 3.5 only names unvested/locked plan securities, the separate 'at any time' ban on third-party derivatives over Company securities (4.7) is not limited by vesting status, so a Restricted Person's hedge of vested, unrestricted shares via a bank-written derivative is independently and absolutely prohibited.

Absolute ban 'under any circumstances' on entering a margin lending arrangement or transferring Company securities into an existing margin loan account; expressly does not extend to other secured funding arrangements.

rules.detail: The outright margin lending ban (4.6) binds only Restricted Persons; however, a forced sale specifically under a margin lending agreement (unlike other secured-lender enforcement) is not excluded from the short-term dealing ban for non-Restricted Employees.

The margin lending ban is expressly confined to margin loans and margin loan accounts; other funding arrangements using Company securities as security are expressly stated not to be restricted by this clause, though the underlying derivative or dealing components of any such arrangement remain subject to 4.4/4.7.

Ban on speculative or short-term dealing, defined to include buying and selling on market within 3 months and other short-term dealings such as forward contracts (naming the very instrument type often used to monetise a holding); vesting-related sales within 3 months of vesting are carved out.
rules.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative or short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a three month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

clearance.evidence: Employees must not deal in (that is, apply for, acquire or dispose of) the Company's securities if: they are aware of Inside Information in relation to the Company; or the Company has notified Employees that they must not deal in securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not deal at any time in financial products such as derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps, contracts for difference or other financial products issued or created over or associated with Company securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Directors and KMP are absolutely banned from any third-party derivative over Company securities, with no clearance or exemption route (other than a listed-portfolio/index carve-out), which directly and completely prohibits the put and call legs of a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing other than margin loans expressly permitted
bespoke_clauses.clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where Company securities may be included as security.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the derivatives ban, the margin lending prohibition is expressly confined to margin loans; a loan secured on the collared shares that is not classified as a margin loan is not itself prohibited for Restricted Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An exception applies where Company securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only an exchange-traded fund or index product containing Company securities as one component escapes the derivatives ban; a bespoke single-stock OTC collar with a bank does not qualify.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forward contracts named as short-term dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a three month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forward contracts are separately flagged as an example of prohibited short-term dealing for all Employees, so even setting aside the Restricted Persons derivatives ban, a forward-style monetisation risks being independently characterised as short-term/speculative dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring a collar or loan to avoid the letter of the margin lending or derivatives bans would not avoid the restriction if its economic substance is a hedge or a margin loan.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for PointsBet's Restricted Persons (Directors and other KMP), the natural client base for such a facility. Section 4.7 imposes an absolute ban on Restricted Persons dealing 'at any time' in any third-party financial product - expressly including options, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference - created over Company securities, with no clearance mechanism and only a narrow listed-portfolio/index exception that a bespoke bank collar would not satisfy; hedging of unvested or holding-locked plan securities is separately and absolutely banned for all Employees under 3.5. By contrast, the loan leg is comparatively unconstrained: the margin lending ban in 4.6 is expressly limited to margin loans and margin loan accounts, and the Policy expressly states that other funding arrangements using Company securities as security are not restricted, so a secured loan (provided it is not classified as a margin loan) is not itself prohibited. Even transactions not caught by the derivatives ban require prior written approval (from the CEO, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee depending on seniority) outside the six annual Blackout Periods, valid for only 5 business days, and the Company applies a substance-over-form approach that would treat an economically equivalent structure the same as a named derivative or margin loan. Consequently, while a bank-secured loan against vested, unrestricted shares appears achievable in isolation, the option legs of a collar cannot be implemented for Directors or KMP under this policy.
